ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus kazirangaensis* is a medium-sized gecko (SVL ~75 mm) with a brown dorsum featuring dark transverse bands. It is distinguished by 18–20 subdigital lamellae and 16–18 precloacal pores.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus kazirangaensis* is distinguished by a unique pattern of 5–6 dark brown, irregular transverse bands on the dorsum that are narrower than the interspaces.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus kazirangaensis* inhabits the tropical moist deciduous forests of Kaziranga National Park, typically found on tree trunks within low-elevation alluvial plains.
ai.behavior: *Cyrtodactylus kazirangaensis* is a strictly nocturnal gecko that remains active at night, foraging for small insects on tree trunks and rocky surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus kazirangaensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus kazirangaensis* is endemic to the Kaziranga National Park in the state of Assam, India, occurring at low elevations within the Brahmaputra River valley.
